referents.why: 'Of us' (first plural) in 'our unrighteousness' is Paul and his readers; no first-plural candidate.
Interrogative 'what' in 'what shall we say': refers to nothing; no neuter singular candidate.
'We' in 'what shall we say' is Paul and his readers; no first-plural candidate.
'I speak' (first singular) is the writer's own remark about how he speaks; no first-person candidate.

links.why: Reversed: the protasis cl1 is the condition, and the question cl0 is what it conditions.
'What shall we say, if our unrighteousness highlights God's righteousness?' cl0 is conditioned by cl1.
The participle 'inflicting the wrath' describes God in the objection; it is not a conjunct of 'what shall we say'.
The articular participle (the one inflicting wrath) is a relative-like clause nested in the noun phrase 'God'.
'What shall we say?' introduces the objection that follows: is God unjust to inflict wrath?

groups.why: The protasis is cl1 and the question it conditions is cl0.
'What shall we say' introduces the objection, which is its part (ruling R1). No sender or addressee is a candidate.

none_fit.what: A remark on the manner of the writer's own speaking ('in human terms'); no link type records a qualification of one's own saying.

none_fit.where: cl4 (κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω, 'I speak in human terms')
none_fit.what: A parenthetical disclaimer about the manner of the argument; no link type relates a comment on one's own argument. Left unlinked.
A parenthetical qualifier of the writer's own speech; no link type records it, so it is left unlinked.

cant_tell.why: A verse-opening 'but' has no host in its own verse, so no contrast with 3:4 is drawn.
A turn needs a sender from the candidates; the speaker 'we' is not offered, so no turn is built.

cant_tell.what: Sender of the turn (the 'we' of 'what shall we say?')
cant_tell.why: The 'we' is the diatribe's speaker and is not offered as a candidate; the turn has no sender.
Contrast with a verse-opening 'but' has no host in its own verse; no link added.
